purpose: Scoring-region geometry for marker-position recognition on the Arche Nova playmat.

geometry_method.attractiveness: Cell centers detected from the original high-resolution scoring imagery; cell boundaries are midpoints between adjacent printed scoring cells. Regions are quadrilaterals.
geometry_method.conservation: Pentagonal regions derived from the original green scoring fields and their exact spans over attractiveness cells. Values 16-11 span 3 attractiveness cells, 10-1 span 2, value 0 is the terminal field.
geometry_method.reputation: Six/eight-vertex polygons traced from the original reputation-track field geometry. Field 1 has 6 vertices; fields 2-15 have 8.
geometry_method.marked_reference_usage: Markiert(1).jpg was used only for validation of the example values, not to derive the polygon coordinates.

classification.tie_breaker: nearest polygon centroid if numerical/registration tolerance causes more than one match
classification.outside_policy: return null and confidence 0 rather than snapping to a field

validation.result: All nine example regions align with the independently derived field geometry in the master coordinate system.
notes: Attractiveness 61 independently resolves to x≈1675..1771 px; the annotation lies at x≈1674..1777 px.
Conservation 6 independently resolves to x≈2668..2856 px; the annotation lies at x≈2670..2849 px.
Conservation 17 independently resolves to x≈290..598 px; the annotation lies inside that field at x≈306..588 px.
Reputation fields 1, 8 and 12 visually match the annotated outlines after mapping the marked image into master coordinates.

revision.method: Each changed reputation field was measured locally from its visible printed boundary in the master reference. No equal-width or equal-spacing model was used. The explicitly marked example fields 1,2,3,8,12 remain byte-for-byte geometrically equivalent to their v1 definitions.
